CHN.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Hold our posture and keep channels open — signal willingness to talk on IP protection and to raise purchases from the United States, but do not preemptively concede or escalate before Washington actually imposes Section 301 tariffs. Present ourselves as the defender of the multilateral WTO order while quietly addressing the specific concerns (technology transfer, market access) that would blunt a broader US action.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: What drives the threat reading (+0.4): the dispute is clearly building against China. The US initiated a Section 301 investigation into China's IP/technology-transfer practices (timeline 2017-08-14), the Trump administration has already imposed Section 201 safeguard tariffs on solar panels and washing machines that hit Chinese suppliers (timeline 2018-01-22), and reporting before the decision date warns of 'significant'/'trillion-dollar range' retaliatory tariff remedies with findings due by August 2018 (Orrick, Jan 2018; Newsweek, Jan 2018). Washington has re-labelled China a 'strategic competitor' and its record US$275.8bn bilateral surplus (65% of China's total surplus) makes China an obvious target (SCMP/Xinhua, Jan 2018). At the same time, the threat is not yet existential: as of 2018-03-01 no broad Section 301 tariffs have been imposed, Chinese exports are still strong (+10.9% y/y in December), and the macro economy shows no financial stress. What justifies the action stance (+0.1, negotiate): China is the surplus country and would lose most from an escalating trade war (SCMP citing Pettis), so maximal escalation would be self-harming. Our best leverage is measured engagement — accept some near-term concessions (deeper IP enforcement, more US purchases) to relieve pressure, while keeping the door open to prove we defend rule-based trade. Escalating now would hand Washington the pretext for the broad tariff action it is already preparing.
key_factors: Section 301 investigation into China IP/tech-transfer ongoing, findings due Aug 2018, broad tariff remedies telegraphed
Section 201 tariffs on solar/washing machines already imposed Jan 2018, hitting Chinese suppliers
Record US$275.8bn China-US trade surplus makes China a natural target
No broad Section 301 tariff actually imposed yet; exports still strong (+10.9% y/y)
US re-labelled China a 'strategic competitor'; Comprehensive Economic Dialogue reportedly suspended
China's Ministry of Commerce threatens 'all necessary measures' but favours dialogue
As surplus country, China loses most from an escalating trade war — escalation self-harming

sources_cited.excerpt: Trump signs memorandum directing USTR to investigate China's IP and technology-transfer practices under Section 301. USTR investigation initiated.
Trump approves Section 201 safeguard tariffs on solar panels and washing machines (China among suppliers hit). First major tariff action.
USTR to announce affirmative finding and make remedy recommendations; many predict broad retaliatory tariffs.
Reports that 301 remedies could include 'significant' tariffs 'in the trillion-dollar range.'
China's trade surplus with US hit record US$275.8bn in 2017, ~65% of China's total global surplus; CED reportedly suspended; trade war 'terrible for surplus countries.'
Exports to US climbed 14.5% in 2017; MOFCOM says imbalance due to economic structure; 'global protectionism on the rise.'
